quote: After a challenging prior period marked by volatile US trade policy, stagnant chemical prices, and pronounced inflationary cost pressures (including across wages, freight and warehousing), Redox staged a resilient operational recovery in FY26. Ongoing dislocations in global supply chains and shifting chemical price dynamics play to the company's strength to leverage its scale and extensive product sourcing network. Even during the toughest distribution environments, the company has proven its ability to win new clients and take market share. The shares are trading at 20x forward earnings, backed by a healthy balance sheet of $132.7 million in net cash, representing roughly 6.8% of its market cap. Because Redox is family controlled and highly aligned with shareholders, the management team have been able to consistently take a patient, disciplined approach to capital allocation. Rather than rushing to purchase the next thing that is available, which we've seen other distribution companies do, they are taking their time to target businesses that offer cultural and strategic alignment, ensuring that any future M&A acts as a catalyst for long term compounding.

headline: Lakehouse Capital modestly increased its Redox holding, viewing recent cost pressures as a one-off reset at an undemanding 14.3x forward earnings
reasoning: Redox delivered mixed results in a challenging operating environment, with volumes growing 13% in the first half despite soft macro conditions, reflecting continued market share gains. Profitability came under pressure due to higher employee and transport costs, while the early-stage US operations remain lumpy due to large customer order patterns. Management continues to strengthen supplier relationships with Dow and Viva Energy, and pursued bolt-on acquisitions like Molekulis to broaden its addressable market. Lakehouse views the cost increases as a one-off reset and expects operating leverage to improve as the full-year cost base becomes clearer and the pricing environment stabilises. At 14.3x forward earnings with 10% of market cap in net cash, the valuation is considered undemanding, and Lakehouse modestly increased its holding.
quote: Encouragingly, volumes grew 13% in the first half despite softer macroeconomic conditions, reflecting continued market share gains. That said, profitability came under pressure due to higher employee and transport costs, while the US operations -- still in their early phase -- remain somewhat uneven, with larger customer orders contributing to lumpiness. The founding family-led management continues to execute well, strengthening supplier relationships with the likes of Dow and Viva Energy, while selectively pursuing bolt-on acquisitions, such as Molekulis, to broaden its addressable market. Looking forward, we believe Redox is well positioned following what we view as a one-off cost reset. With a clearer view of the full-year cost base, we expect operating leverage to improve over time. Importantly, the pricing environment has stabilised, providing a better platform for volume growth to drive top-line momentum. At 14.3x forward earnings and with 10% of its market capitalisation in net cash, the valuation is undemanding. With expectations now more balanced, we've taken the opportunity to modestly increase our holding.
